definition: doing what a person in authority tells you to do
example: Our first subject is obedience.

definition: a person who offers to take part in something without being forced
example: You are a volunteer for a study of memory.

definition: accepted as having the right to give orders or make decisions
example: Yale is a famous and legitimate institution.

definition: a person who secretly works with the researcher while pretending to be an ordinary participant
example: In fact he is a confederate: an actor who works for the experimenter.

definition: to pause before you do something because you are not sure
example: If you hesitate, the experimenter answers with a prod.

definition: a short push; here, a standard sentence that tells someone to go on
example: The experimenter answers with a prod.

definition: strong feelings of worry, pain or unhappiness
example: Many volunteers showed clear distress.

definition: making someone believe something that is not true
example: The whole study relied on deception.

definition: doubting whether something is true or good
example: Be sceptical of the headline and of its critics.

definition: the health, safety and happiness of a person or group
example: Her main objection was about the volunteers' welfare.

definition: a person's agreement to take part after being told honestly what will happen
example: They had not given real informed consent.

definition: to explain the true purpose of a study to participants after it has finished
example: Every volunteer was told the truth in a debrief.

definition: a request that speaks to a person's values or feelings
example: Appeals to the value of science worked better than orders.

definition: a collection of old documents and records
example: A third kind of criticism came from the archive.

definition: a version of a procedure in which one thing is changed
example: Milgram ran about twenty variations of the study.

definition: a rule or measure that protects people from harm
example: Stopping at 150 volts was a reasonable safeguard.

definition: statistically significant: unlikely to be caused by chance alone
example: The difference was not statistically significant.

definition: a new study that repeats an earlier study to check its result
example: This is a partial replication.

definition: a warning that a statement is only true under certain conditions
example: Every claim needs a caveat.

definition: a statement that something is true, especially one that is not yet proved
example: Let us test some claims.
